sources.entry: pyenv-win - A Python version manager for Windows (rbenv-win fork).

summary.one_liner: A Windows port of rbenv, the Ruby version manager, for installing and switching between Ruby versions from the command line.
summary.what_it_does: The README describes rbenv for Windows as a port of the original rbenv tool. It provides an `rbenv` command with a `commands` subcommand that lists the implemented commands. Some rbenv commands are not implemented, though the README says this is not a problem for basic use. Installation is done by cloning the repository into the USERPROFILE directory and adding its bin and shims directories to the PATH. Once installed, `rbenv install`, `rbenv global`, and `rbenv rehash` are used to set up a Ruby version. For detailed command usage, the README refers readers to the original rbenv documentation. The repository is listed in awesome-python under Microsoft Windows as a fork of pyenv-win, though the README itself does not describe Python support.
use_cases: install and switch Ruby versions on Windows
manage multiple Ruby versions per user
set a global Ruby version on Windows
port rbenv workflows to a Windows machine
how_to_run: Add %USERPROFILE%\.rbenv-win\bin and %USERPROFILE%\.rbenv-win\shims to the PATH (see README for setx command)
notable: Windows port of the rbenv Ruby version manager
Installs into the USERPROFILE directory with a PATH setup step
Documentation for detailed commands defers to the original rbenv project
Includes a test.bat release test procedure
caveats: Some rbenv commands are not implemented
Setup requires manually editing the PATH environment variable
The README gives no list of implemented commands beyond the `rbenv commands` output
